correctness.rationale: For any connected allocation, N tr[(L+J)^(-1)-J] is strictly convex in individual edge weights. Graph automorphism averaging is therefore sufficient and the global optimizer unique. Grounded clique inversion and bridge additivity prove \(K=A/c+C/a+D/(a+mb)\). Three-term weighted Cauchy-Schwarz proves the inner price branch and equality feasibility \(t\le4(m+1)/(2m+1)\); at higher price the exact boundary optimum has nonnegative KKT slack \(m(m-1)((2m+1)t-4(m+1))/a^2\) and strict convexity proves uniqueness. The attached exact SymPy checker passed all 628 assertion groups, including direct Laplacian pseudoinverses \(2\le m\le5\); finite checks only corroborate the analytical theorem.

originality.rationale: The original 2006 and 2008 Ghosh-Boyd-Saberi barbell solution uses unit price on every edge, corresponding to the single \(t=1\) slice, and derives the general convex reduction. The new claim specifies a nonconstant peripheral link price for all \(t>0\), and an exact global support transition \(t_c(m)=4(m+1)/(2m+1)\). Earlier inspected work did not state or imply the all-price classification merely by its stated fixed-price optimum. This is an originality assessment under best-known accessible literature, not a uniqueness certification.

value.rationale: Variable material cost on redundant within-community links is a natural engineering constraint. The theorem identifies exactly when a network of two dense clusters should be optimally implemented as a two-star bridge, computes all actual edge conductances and the full budget-resistance frontier for any clique size, and shows complete insensitivity to any further peripheral price increase. The cutoff varies nontrivially with cluster size and is not inferred from the known single \(t=1\) optimum. It is a structural graph-support transition, not a selected narrow arithmetic invariant.
